12 /-!
13 # Affine spaces
14 
15 This file defines affine subspaces (over modules) and the affine span of a set of points.
16 
17 ## Main definitions
18 
19 * `AffineSubspace k P` is the type of affine subspaces. Unlike affine spaces, affine subspaces are
20   allowed to be empty, and lemmas that do not apply to empty affine subspaces have `Nonempty`
21   hypotheses. There is a `CompleteLattice` structure on affine subspaces.
22 * `AffineSubspace.direction` gives the `Submodule` spanned by the pairwise differences of points
23   in an `AffineSubspace`. There are various lemmas relating to the set of vectors in the
24   `direction`, and relating the lattice structure on affine subspaces to that on their directions.
25 * `affineSpan` gives the affine subspace spanned by a set of points, with `vectorSpan` giving its
26   direction. The `affineSpan` is defined in terms of `spanPoints`, which gives an explicit
27   description of the points contained in the affine span; `spanPoints` itself should generally only
28   be used when that description is required, with `affineSpan` being the main definition for other
29   purposes. Two other descriptions of the affine span are proved equivalent: it is the `sInf` of
30   affine subspaces containing the points, and (if `[Nontrivial k]`) it contains exactly those points
31   that are affine combinations of points in the given set.
32 
33 ## Implementation notes
34 
35 `outParam` is used in the definition of `AddTorsor V P` to make `V` an implicit argument (deduced
36 from `P`) in most cases. As for modules, `k` is an explicit argument rather than implied by `P` or
37 `V`.
38 
39 This file only provides purely algebraic definitions and results. Those depending on analysis or
40 topology are defined elsewhere; see `Analysis.Normed.Affine.AddTorsor` and
41 `Topology.Algebra.Affine`.
42 
43 ## References
44 
45 * https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Affine_space
46 * https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Principal_homogeneous_space

59 variable (k : Type*) {V : Type*} {P : Type*} [Ring k] [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V]

62 /-- The submodule spanning the differences of a (possibly empty) set of points. -/
63 def vectorSpan (s : Set P) : Submodule k V :=
64   Submodule.span k (s -ᵥ s)
65 
66 /-- The definition of `vectorSpan`, for rewriting. -/
67 theorem vectorSpan_def (s : Set P) : vectorSpan k s = Submodule.span k (s -ᵥ s) :=
68   rfl
69 
70 /-- `vectorSpan` is monotone. -/
71 theorem vectorSpan_mono {s₁ s₂ : Set P} (h : s₁ ⊆ s₂) : vectorSpan k s₁ ≤ vectorSpan k s₂ :=
72   Submodule.span_mono (vsub_self_mono h)
73 
74 variable (P) in
75 /-- The `vectorSpan` of the empty set is `⊥`. -/
76 @[simp]
77 theorem vectorSpan_empty : vectorSpan k (∅ : Set P) = (⊥ : Submodule k V) := by
78   rw [vectorSpan_def, vsub_empty, Submodule.span_empty]
79 
80 /-- The `vectorSpan` of a single point is `⊥`. -/
81 @[simp]
82 theorem vectorSpan_singleton (p : P) : vectorSpan k ({p} : Set P) = ⊥ := by simp [vectorSpan_def]
83 
84 /-- The `s -ᵥ s` lies within the `vectorSpan k s`. -/
85 theorem vsub_set_subset_vectorSpan (s : Set P) : s -ᵥ s ⊆ ↑(vectorSpan k s) :=
86   Submodule.subset_span
87 
88 /-- Each pairwise difference is in the `vectorSpan`. -/
89 theorem vsub_mem_vectorSpan {s : Set P} {p₁ p₂ : P} (hp₁ : p₁ ∈ s) (hp₂ : p₂ ∈ s) :
90     p₁ -ᵥ p₂ ∈ vectorSpan k s :=
91   vsub_set_subset_vectorSpan k s (vsub_mem_vsub hp₁ hp₂)
92 
93 lemma vectorSpan_of_subsingleton {s : Set P} (h : s.Subsingleton) : vectorSpan k s = ⊥ := by
94   rcases h.eq_empty_or_singleton with rfl | ⟨p, rfl⟩ <;> simp
95 
96 @[simp]
97 lemma vectorSpan_eq_bot_iff_subsingleton {s : Set P} : vectorSpan k s = ⊥ ↔ s.Subsingleton := by
98   refine ⟨fun h ↦ ?_, vectorSpan_of_subsingleton _⟩
99   by_contra hns
100   rw [Set.not_subsingleton_iff] at hns
101   obtain ⟨p, hp, q, hq, hpq⟩ := hns
102   have hpq' := vsub_mem_vectorSpan k hp hq
103   simp_all
104 
105 /-- The points in the affine span of a (possibly empty) set of points. Use `affineSpan` instead to
106 get an `AffineSubspace k P`. -/
107 def spanPoints (s : Set P) : Set P :=
108   { p | ∃ p₁ ∈ s, ∃ v ∈ vectorSpan k s, p = v +ᵥ p₁ }
109 
110 /-- A point in a set is in its affine span. -/
111 theorem mem_spanPoints (p : P) (s : Set P) : p ∈ s → p ∈ spanPoints k s
112   | hp => ⟨p, hp, 0, Submodule.zero_mem _, (zero_vadd V p).symm⟩
113 
114 /-- A set is contained in its `spanPoints`. -/
115 theorem subset_spanPoints (s : Set P) : s ⊆ spanPoints k s := fun p => mem_spanPoints k p s
116 
117 /-- The `spanPoints` of a set is nonempty if and only if that set is. -/
118 @[simp]
119 theorem spanPoints_nonempty (s : Set P) : (spanPoints k s).Nonempty ↔ s.Nonempty := by
120   constructor
121   · contrapose
122     rw [Set.not_nonempty_iff_eq_empty, Set.not_nonempty_iff_eq_empty]
123     intro h
124     simp [h, spanPoints]
125   · exact fun h => h.mono (subset_spanPoints _ _)
126 
127 /-- Adding a point in the affine span and a vector in the spanning submodule produces a point in the
128 affine span. -/
129 theorem vadd_mem_spanPoints_of_mem_spanPoints_of_mem_vectorSpan {s : Set P} {p : P} {v : V}
130     (hp : p ∈ spanPoints k s) (hv : v ∈ vectorSpan k s) : v +ᵥ p ∈ spanPoints k s := by
131   rcases hp with ⟨p₂, ⟨hp₂, ⟨v₂, ⟨hv₂, hv₂p⟩⟩⟩⟩
132   rw [hv₂p, vadd_vadd]
133   exact ⟨p₂, hp₂, v + v₂, (vectorSpan k s).add_mem hv hv₂, rfl⟩
134 
135 /-- Subtracting two points in the affine span produces a vector in the spanning submodule. -/
136 theorem vsub_mem_vectorSpan_of_mem_spanPoints_of_mem_spanPoints {s : Set P} {p₁ p₂ : P}
137     (hp₁ : p₁ ∈ spanPoints k s) (hp₂ : p₂ ∈ spanPoints k s) : p₁ -ᵥ p₂ ∈ vectorSpan k s := by
138   rcases hp₁ with ⟨p₁a, ⟨hp₁a, ⟨v₁, ⟨hv₁, hv₁p⟩⟩⟩⟩
139   rcases hp₂ with ⟨p₂a, ⟨hp₂a, ⟨v₂, ⟨hv₂, hv₂p⟩⟩⟩⟩
140   rw [hv₁p, hv₂p, vsub_vadd_eq_vsub_sub (v₁ +ᵥ p₁a), vadd_vsub_assoc, add_comm, add_sub_assoc]
141   have hv₁v₂ : v₁ - v₂ ∈ vectorSpan k s := (vectorSpan k s).sub_mem hv₁ hv₂
142   refine (vectorSpan k s).add_mem ?_ hv₁v₂
143   exact vsub_mem_vectorSpan k hp₁a hp₂a
144 
145 end

147 /-- An `AffineSubspace k P` is a subset of an `AffineSpace V P` that, if not empty, has an affine
148 space structure induced by a corresponding subspace of the `Module k V`. -/
149 structure AffineSubspace (k : Type*) {V : Type*} (P : Type*) [Ring k] [AddCommGroup V]
150   [Module k V] [AffineSpace V P] where
151   /-- The affine subspace seen as a subset. -/
152   carrier : Set P
153   smul_vsub_vadd_mem :
154     ∀ (c : k) {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P},
155       p₁ ∈ carrier → p₂ ∈ carrier → p₃ ∈ carrier → c • (p₁ -ᵥ p₂ : V) +ᵥ p₃ ∈ carrier
156

158 
159 variable {k V : Type*} [Ring k] [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V]
160 
161 /-- Reinterpret `p : Submodule k V` as an `AffineSubspace k V`. -/
162 def toAffineSubspace (p : Submodule k V) : AffineSubspace k V where
163   carrier := p
164   smul_vsub_vadd_mem _ _ _ _ h₁ h₂ h₃ := p.add_mem (p.smul_mem _ (p.sub_mem h₁ h₂)) h₃
165 
166 end Submodule

168 namespace AffineSubspace

170 variable (k : Type*) {V : Type*} (P : Type*) [Ring k] [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V]
171   [AffineSpace V P]
172 
173 instance : SetLike (AffineSubspace k P) P where
174   coe := carrier
175   coe_injective' p q _ := by cases p; cases q; congr
176 
177 instance : PartialOrder (AffineSubspace k P) := .ofSetLike (AffineSubspace k P) P
178 
179 /-- A point is in an affine subspace coerced to a set if and only if it is in that affine
180 subspace. -/
181 theorem mem_coe (p : P) (s : AffineSubspace k P) : p ∈ (s : Set P) ↔ p ∈ s := by simp
182 
183 variable {k P}
184 
185 /-- The direction of an affine subspace is the submodule spanned by
186 the pairwise differences of points.  (Except in the case of an empty
187 affine subspace, where the direction is the zero submodule, every
188 vector in the direction is the difference of two points in the affine
189 subspace.) -/
190 def direction (s : AffineSubspace k P) : Submodule k V :=
191   vectorSpan k (s : Set P)
192 
193 /-- The direction equals the `vectorSpan`. -/
194 theorem direction_eq_vectorSpan (s : AffineSubspace k P) : s.direction = vectorSpan k (s : Set P) :=
195   rfl
196 
197 /-- Alternative definition of the direction when the affine subspace is nonempty. This is defined so
198 that the order on submodules (as used in the definition of `Submodule.span`) can be used in the
199 proof of `coe_direction_eq_vsub_set`, and is not intended to be used beyond that proof. -/
200 def directionOfNonempty {s : AffineSubspace k P} (h : (s : Set P).Nonempty) : Submodule k V where
201   carrier := (s : Set P) -ᵥ s
202   zero_mem' := by
203     obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ := h
204     exact vsub_self p ▸ vsub_mem_vsub hp hp
205   add_mem' := by
206     rintro _ _ ⟨p₁, hp₁, p₂, hp₂, rfl⟩ ⟨p₃, hp₃, p₄, hp₄, rfl⟩
207     rw [← vadd_vsub_assoc]
208     refine vsub_mem_vsub ?_ hp₄
209     convert s.smul_vsub_vadd_mem 1 hp₁ hp₂ hp₃
210     rw [one_smul]
211   smul_mem' := by
212     rintro c _ ⟨p₁, hp₁, p₂, hp₂, rfl⟩
213     rw [← vadd_vsub (c • (p₁ -ᵥ p₂)) p₂]
214     refine vsub_mem_vsub ?_ hp₂
215     exact s.smul_vsub_vadd_mem c hp₁ hp₂ hp₂
216 
217 /-- `direction_of_nonempty` gives the same submodule as `direction`. -/
218 theorem directionOfNonempty_eq_direction {s : AffineSubspace k P} (h : (s : Set P).Nonempty) :
219     directionOfNonempty h = s.direction := by
220   refine le_antisymm ?_ (Submodule.span_le.2 Set.Subset.rfl)
221   rw [← SetLike.coe_subset_coe, directionOfNonempty, direction, Submodule.coe_set_mk,
222     AddSubmonoid.coe_set_mk]
223   exact vsub_set_subset_vectorSpan k _
224 
225 /-- The set of vectors in the direction of a nonempty affine subspace is given by `vsub_set`. -/
226 theorem coe_direction_eq_vsub_set {s : AffineSubspace k P} (h : (s : Set P).Nonempty) :
227     (s.direction : Set V) = (s : Set P) -ᵥ s :=
228   directionOfNonempty_eq_direction h ▸ rfl
229 
230 /-- A vector is in the direction of a nonempty affine subspace if and only if it is the subtraction
231 of two vectors in the subspace. -/
232 theorem mem_direction_iff_eq_vsub {s : AffineSubspace k P} (h : (s : Set P).Nonempty) (v : V) :
233     v ∈ s.direction ↔ ∃ p₁ ∈ s, ∃ p₂ ∈ s, v = p₁ -ᵥ p₂ := by
234   rw [← SetLike.mem_coe, coe_direction_eq_vsub_set h, Set.mem_vsub]
235   simp only [SetLike.mem_coe, eq_comm]
236 
237 /-- Adding a vector in the direction to a point in the subspace produces a point in the
238 subspace. -/
239 theorem vadd_mem_of_mem_direction {s : AffineSubspace k P} {v : V} (hv : v ∈ s.direction) {p : P}
240     (hp : p ∈ s) : v +ᵥ p ∈ s := by
241   rw [mem_direction_iff_eq_vsub ⟨p, hp⟩] at hv
242   rcases hv with ⟨p₁, hp₁, p₂, hp₂, hv⟩
243   rw [hv]
244   convert s.smul_vsub_vadd_mem 1 hp₁ hp₂ hp
245   rw [one_smul]
246 
247 /-- Subtracting two points in the subspace produces a vector in the direction. -/
248 theorem vsub_mem_direction {s : AffineSubspace k P} {p₁ p₂ : P} (hp₁ : p₁ ∈ s) (hp₂ : p₂ ∈ s) :
249     p₁ -ᵥ p₂ ∈ s.direction :=
250   vsub_mem_vectorSpan k hp₁ hp₂
251 
252 /-- Adding a vector to a point in a subspace produces a point in the subspace if and only if the
253 vector is in the direction. -/
254 theorem vadd_mem_iff_mem_direction {s : AffineSubspace k P} (v : V) {p : P} (hp : p ∈ s) :
255     v +ᵥ p ∈ s ↔ v ∈ s.direction :=
256   ⟨fun h => by simpa using vsub_mem_direction h hp, fun h => vadd_mem_of_mem_direction h hp⟩
257 
258 /-- Adding a vector in the direction to a point produces a point in the subspace if and only if
259 the original point is in the subspace. -/
260 theorem vadd_mem_iff_mem_of_mem_direction {s : AffineSubspace k P} {v : V} (hv : v ∈ s.direction)
261     {p : P} : v +ᵥ p ∈ s ↔ p ∈ s := by
262   refine ⟨fun h => ?_, fun h => vadd_mem_of_mem_direction hv h⟩
263   convert vadd_mem_of_mem_direction (Submodule.neg_mem _ hv) h
264   simp
265 
266 /-- Given a point in an affine subspace, the set of vectors in its direction equals the set of
267 vectors subtracting that point on the right. -/
268 theorem coe_direction_eq_vsub_set_right {s : AffineSubspace k P} {p : P} (hp : p ∈ s) :
269     (s.direction : Set V) = (· -ᵥ p) '' s := by
270   rw [coe_direction_eq_vsub_set ⟨p, hp⟩]
271   refine le_antisymm ?_ ?_
272   · rintro v ⟨p₁, hp₁, p₂, hp₂, rfl⟩
273     exact ⟨(p₁ -ᵥ p₂) +ᵥ p,
274       vadd_mem_of_mem_direction (vsub_mem_direction hp₁ hp₂) hp, vadd_vsub _ _⟩
275   · rintro v ⟨p₂, hp₂, rfl⟩
276     exact ⟨p₂, hp₂, p, hp, rfl⟩
277 
278 /-- Given a point in an affine subspace, the set of vectors in its direction equals the set of
279 vectors subtracting that point on the left. -/
280 theorem coe_direction_eq_vsub_set_left {s : AffineSubspace k P} {p : P} (hp : p ∈ s) :
281     (s.direction : Set V) = (p -ᵥ ·) '' s := by
282   ext v
283   rw [SetLike.mem_coe, ← Submodule.neg_mem_iff, ← SetLike.mem_coe,
284     coe_direction_eq_vsub_set_right hp, Set.mem_image, Set.mem_image]
285   conv_lhs =>
286     congr
287     ext
288     rw [← neg_vsub_eq_vsub_rev, neg_inj]
289 
290 /-- Given a point in an affine subspace, a vector is in its direction if and only if it results from
291 subtracting that point on the right. -/
292 theorem mem_direction_iff_eq_vsub_right {s : AffineSubspace k P} {p : P} (hp : p ∈ s) (v : V) :
293     v ∈ s.direction ↔ ∃ p₂ ∈ s, v = p₂ -ᵥ p := by
294   rw [← SetLike.mem_coe, coe_direction_eq_vsub_set_right hp]
295   exact ⟨fun ⟨p₂, hp₂, hv⟩ => ⟨p₂, hp₂, hv.symm⟩, fun ⟨p₂, hp₂, hv⟩ => ⟨p₂, hp₂, hv.symm⟩⟩
296 
297 /-- Given a point in an affine subspace, a vector is in its direction if and only if it results from
298 subtracting that point on the left. -/
299 theorem mem_direction_iff_eq_vsub_left {s : AffineSubspace k P} {p : P} (hp : p ∈ s) (v : V) :
300     v ∈ s.direction ↔ ∃ p₂ ∈ s, v = p -ᵥ p₂ := by
301   rw [← SetLike.mem_coe, coe_direction_eq_vsub_set_left hp]
302   exact ⟨fun ⟨p₂, hp₂, hv⟩ => ⟨p₂, hp₂, hv.symm⟩, fun ⟨p₂, hp₂, hv⟩ => ⟨p₂, hp₂, hv.symm⟩⟩
303 
304 /-- Two affine subspaces are equal if they have the same points. -/
305 theorem coe_injective : Function.Injective ((↑) : AffineSubspace k P → Set P) :=
306   SetLike.coe_injective
307 
308 @[ext (iff := false)]
309 theorem ext {p q : AffineSubspace k P} (h : ∀ x, x ∈ p ↔ x ∈ q) : p = q :=
310   SetLike.ext h
311 
312 protected theorem ext_iff (s₁ s₂ : AffineSubspace k P) : s₁ = s₂ ↔ (s₁ : Set P) = s₂ :=
313   SetLike.ext'_iff
314 
315 /-- Two affine subspaces with the same direction and nonempty intersection are equal. -/
316 theorem ext_of_direction_eq {s₁ s₂ : AffineSubspace k P} (hd : s₁.direction = s₂.direction)
317     (hn : ((s₁ : Set P) ∩ s₂).Nonempty) : s₁ = s₂ := by
318   ext p
319   have hq1 := Set.mem_of_mem_inter_left hn.some_mem
320   have hq2 := Set.mem_of_mem_inter_right hn.some_mem
321   constructor
322   · intro hp
323     rw [← vsub_vadd p hn.some]
324     refine vadd_mem_of_mem_direction ?_ hq2
325     rw [← hd]
326     exact vsub_mem_direction hp hq1
327   · intro hp
328     rw [← vsub_vadd p hn.some]
329     refine vadd_mem_of_mem_direction ?_ hq1
330     rw [hd]
331     exact vsub_mem_direction hp hq2
332 
333 /-- Two affine subspaces with nonempty intersection are equal if and only if their directions are
334 equal. -/
335 theorem eq_iff_direction_eq_of_mem {s₁ s₂ : AffineSubspace k P} {p : P} (h₁ : p ∈ s₁)
336     (h₂ : p ∈ s₂) : s₁ = s₂ ↔ s₁.direction = s₂.direction :=
337   ⟨fun h => h ▸ rfl, fun h => ext_of_direction_eq h ⟨p, h₁, h₂⟩⟩
338 
339 /-- Construct an affine subspace from a point and a direction. -/
340 def mk' (p : P) (direction : Submodule k V) : AffineSubspace k P where
341   carrier := { q | q -ᵥ p ∈ direction }
342   smul_vsub_vadd_mem c p₁ p₂ p₃ hp₁ hp₂ hp₃ := by
343     simpa [vadd_vsub_assoc] using
344       direction.add_mem (direction.smul_mem c (direction.sub_mem hp₁ hp₂)) hp₃
345 
346 /-- A point lies in an affine subspace constructed from another point and a direction if and only
347 if their difference is in that direction. -/
348 @[simp]
349 theorem mem_mk' {p q : P} {direction : Submodule k V} : q ∈ mk' p direction ↔ q -ᵥ p ∈ direction :=
350   Iff.rfl
351 
352 /-- An affine subspace constructed from a point and a direction contains that point. -/
353 theorem self_mem_mk' (p : P) (direction : Submodule k V) : p ∈ mk' p direction := by
354   simp
355 
356 /-- An affine subspace constructed from a point and a direction contains the result of adding a
357 vector in that direction to that point. -/
358 theorem vadd_mem_mk' {v : V} (p : P) {direction : Submodule k V} (hv : v ∈ direction) :
359     v +ᵥ p ∈ mk' p direction := by
360   simpa
361 
362 /-- An affine subspace constructed from a point and a direction is nonempty. -/
363 theorem mk'_nonempty (p : P) (direction : Submodule k V) : (mk' p direction : Set P).Nonempty :=
364   ⟨p, self_mem_mk' p direction⟩
365 
366 instance (p : P) (direction : Submodule k V) : Nonempty (mk' p direction) :=
367   ⟨⟨p, self_mem_mk' p direction⟩⟩
368 
369 /-- The direction of an affine subspace constructed from a point and a direction. -/
370 @[simp]
371 theorem direction_mk' (p : P) (direction : Submodule k V) :
372     (mk' p direction).direction = direction := by
373   ext v
374   rw [mem_direction_iff_eq_vsub (mk'_nonempty _ _)]
375   constructor
376   · rintro ⟨p₁, hp₁, p₂, hp₂, rfl⟩
377     simpa using direction.sub_mem hp₁ hp₂
378   · exact fun hv => ⟨v +ᵥ p, vadd_mem_mk' _ hv, p, self_mem_mk' _ _, (vadd_vsub _ _).symm⟩
379 
380 /-- Constructing an affine subspace from a point in a subspace and that subspace's direction
381 yields the original subspace. -/
382 @[simp]
383 theorem mk'_eq {s : AffineSubspace k P} {p : P} (hp : p ∈ s) : mk' p s.direction = s :=
384   ext_of_direction_eq (direction_mk' p s.direction) ⟨p, Set.mem_inter (self_mem_mk' _ _) hp⟩
385 
386 /-- If an affine subspace contains a set of points, it contains the `spanPoints` of that set. -/
387 theorem spanPoints_subset_coe_of_subset_coe {s : Set P} {s₁ : AffineSubspace k P} (h : s ⊆ s₁) :
388     spanPoints k s ⊆ s₁ := by
389   rintro p ⟨p₁, hp₁, v, hv, hp⟩
390   rw [hp]
391   have hp₁s₁ : p₁ ∈ (s₁ : Set P) := Set.mem_of_mem_of_subset hp₁ h
392   refine vadd_mem_of_mem_direction ?_ hp₁s₁
393   have hs : vectorSpan k s ≤ s₁.direction := vectorSpan_mono k h
394   rw [SetLike.le_def] at hs
395   rw [← SetLike.mem_coe]
396   exact Set.mem_of_mem_of_subset hv hs
397 
398 end AffineSubspace

404 @[simp]
405 theorem mem_toAffineSubspace {p : Submodule k V} {x : V} :
406     x ∈ p.toAffineSubspace ↔ x ∈ p :=
407   Iff.rfl
408 
409 @[simp]
410 theorem toAffineSubspace_direction (s : Submodule k V) : s.toAffineSubspace.direction = s := by
411   ext x; simp [← s.toAffineSubspace.vadd_mem_iff_mem_direction _ s.zero_mem]

415 section affineSpan
416 
417 variable (k : Type*) {V : Type*} {P : Type*} [Ring k] [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V]
418   [AffineSpace V P]
419 
420 /-- The affine span of a set of points is the smallest affine subspace containing those points.
421 (Actually defined here in terms of spans in modules.) -/
422 def affineSpan (s : Set P) : AffineSubspace k P where
423   carrier := spanPoints k s
424   smul_vsub_vadd_mem c _ _ _ hp₁ hp₂ hp₃ :=
425     vadd_mem_spanPoints_of_mem_spanPoints_of_mem_vectorSpan k hp₃
426       ((vectorSpan k s).smul_mem c
427         (vsub_mem_vectorSpan_of_mem_spanPoints_of_mem_spanPoints k hp₁ hp₂))
428 
429 /-- The affine span, converted to a set, is `spanPoints`. -/
430 @[simp]
431 theorem coe_affineSpan (s : Set P) : (affineSpan k s : Set P) = spanPoints k s :=
432   rfl
433 
434 /-- The condition for a point to be in the affine span, in terms of `vectorSpan`. -/
435 lemma mem_affineSpan_iff_exists {p : P} {s : Set P} : p ∈ affineSpan k s ↔
436     ∃ p₁ ∈ s, ∃ v ∈ vectorSpan k s, p = v +ᵥ p₁ :=
437   Iff.rfl
438 
439 /-- A set is contained in its affine span. -/
440 theorem subset_affineSpan (s : Set P) : s ⊆ affineSpan k s :=
441   subset_spanPoints k s
442 
443 /-- The direction of the affine span is the `vectorSpan`. -/
444 theorem direction_affineSpan (s : Set P) : (affineSpan k s).direction = vectorSpan k s := by
445   apply le_antisymm
446   · refine Submodule.span_le.2 ?_
447     rintro v ⟨p₁, ⟨p₂, hp₂, v₁, hv₁, hp₁⟩, p₃, ⟨p₄, hp₄, v₂, hv₂, hp₃⟩, rfl⟩
448     simp only [SetLike.mem_coe]
449     rw [hp₁, hp₃, vsub_vadd_eq_vsub_sub, vadd_vsub_assoc]
450     exact
451       (vectorSpan k s).sub_mem ((vectorSpan k s).add_mem hv₁ (vsub_mem_vectorSpan k hp₂ hp₄)) hv₂
452   · exact vectorSpan_mono k (subset_spanPoints k s)
453 
454 /-- A point in a set is in its affine span. -/
455 theorem mem_affineSpan {p : P} {s : Set P} (hp : p ∈ s) : p ∈ affineSpan k s :=
456   mem_spanPoints k p s hp
457 
458 @[simp]
459 lemma vectorSpan_add_self (s : Set V) : (vectorSpan k s : Set V) + s = affineSpan k s := by
460   ext
461   simp [mem_add, spanPoints]
462   grind
463 
464 variable {k}
465 
466 /-- Adding a point in the affine span and a vector in the spanning submodule produces a point in the
467 affine span. -/
468 theorem vadd_mem_affineSpan_of_mem_affineSpan_of_mem_vectorSpan {s : Set P} {p : P} {v : V}
469     (hp : p ∈ affineSpan k s) (hv : v ∈ vectorSpan k s) : v +ᵥ p ∈ affineSpan k s :=
470   vadd_mem_spanPoints_of_mem_spanPoints_of_mem_vectorSpan k hp hv
471 
472 /-- Subtracting two points in the affine span produces a vector in the spanning submodule. -/
473 theorem vsub_mem_vectorSpan_of_mem_affineSpan_of_mem_affineSpan {s : Set P} {p₁ p₂ : P}
474     (hp₁ : p₁ ∈ affineSpan k s) (hp₂ : p₂ ∈ affineSpan k s) : p₁ -ᵥ p₂ ∈ vectorSpan k s :=
475   vsub_mem_vectorSpan_of_mem_spanPoints_of_mem_spanPoints k hp₁ hp₂
476 
477 /-- If an affine subspace contains a set of points, it contains the affine span of that set. -/
478 theorem affineSpan_le_of_subset_coe {s : Set P} {s₁ : AffineSubspace k P} (h : s ⊆ s₁) :
479     affineSpan k s ≤ s₁ :=
480   AffineSubspace.spanPoints_subset_coe_of_subset_coe h
481 
482 end affineSpan

484 namespace AffineSubspace
485 
486 variable {k : Type*} {V : Type*} {P : Type*} [Ring k] [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V]
487   [S : AffineSpace V P] {ι : Sort*}
488 
489 instance : CompleteLattice (AffineSubspace k P) where
490   sup := fun s₁ s₂ => affineSpan k (s₁ ∪ s₂)
491   le_sup_left := fun _ _ =>
492     Set.Subset.trans Set.subset_union_left (subset_spanPoints k _)
493   le_sup_right := fun _ _ =>
494     Set.Subset.trans Set.subset_union_right (subset_spanPoints k _)
495   sup_le := fun _ _ _ hs₁ hs₂ => spanPoints_subset_coe_of_subset_coe (Set.union_subset hs₁ hs₂)
496   inf := fun s₁ s₂ =>
497     mk (s₁ ∩ s₂) fun c _ _ _ hp₁ hp₂ hp₃ =>
498       ⟨s₁.smul_vsub_vadd_mem c hp₁.1 hp₂.1 hp₃.1, s₂.smul_vsub_vadd_mem c hp₁.2 hp₂.2 hp₃.2⟩
499   inf_le_left := fun _ _ => Set.inter_subset_left
500   inf_le_right := fun _ _ => Set.inter_subset_right
501   top :=
502     { carrier := Set.univ
503       smul_vsub_vadd_mem := fun _ _ _ _ _ _ _ => Set.mem_univ _ }
504   le_top := fun _ _ _ => Set.mem_univ _
505   bot :=
506     { carrier := ∅
507       smul_vsub_vadd_mem := fun _ _ _ _ => False.elim }
508   bot_le := fun _ _ => False.elim
509   sSup := fun s => affineSpan k (⋃ s' ∈ s, (s' : Set P))
510   sInf := fun s =>
511     mk (⋂ s' ∈ s, (s' : Set P)) fun c p₁ p₂ p₃ hp₁ hp₂ hp₃ =>
512       Set.mem_iInter₂.2 fun s₂ hs₂ => by
513         rw [Set.mem_iInter₂] at *
514         exact s₂.smul_vsub_vadd_mem c (hp₁ s₂ hs₂) (hp₂ s₂ hs₂) (hp₃ s₂ hs₂)
515   isLUB_sSup _ :=
516     ⟨fun _ h => Set.Subset.trans (Set.subset_biUnion_of_mem h) (subset_spanPoints k _),
517       fun _ h => spanPoints_subset_coe_of_subset_coe (Set.iUnion₂_subset h)⟩
518   isGLB_sInf _ := .of_image SetLike.coe_subset_coe isGLB_biInf
519   le_inf := fun _ _ _ => Set.subset_inter
520 
521 instance : Inhabited (AffineSubspace k P) :=
522   ⟨⊤⟩
523 
524 /-- The `≤` order on subspaces is the same as that on the corresponding sets. -/
525 theorem le_def (s₁ s₂ : AffineSubspace k P) : s₁ ≤ s₂ ↔ (s₁ : Set P) ⊆ s₂ :=
526   Iff.rfl
527 
528 /-- One subspace is less than or equal to another if and only if all its points are in the second
529 subspace. -/
530 theorem le_def' (s₁ s₂ : AffineSubspace k P) : s₁ ≤ s₂ ↔ ∀ p ∈ s₁, p ∈ s₂ :=
531   Iff.rfl
532 
533 /-- The `<` order on subspaces is the same as that on the corresponding sets. -/
534 theorem lt_def (s₁ s₂ : AffineSubspace k P) : s₁ < s₂ ↔ (s₁ : Set P) ⊂ s₂ :=
535   Iff.rfl
536 
537 /-- One subspace is not less than or equal to another if and only if it has a point not in the
538 second subspace. -/
539 theorem not_le_iff_exists (s₁ s₂ : AffineSubspace k P) : ¬s₁ ≤ s₂ ↔ ∃ p ∈ s₁, p ∉ s₂ :=
540   Set.not_subset
541 
542 /-- If a subspace is less than another, there is a point only in the second. -/
543 theorem exists_of_lt {s₁ s₂ : AffineSubspace k P} (h : s₁ < s₂) : ∃ p ∈ s₂, p ∉ s₁ :=
544   Set.exists_of_ssubset h
545 
546 /-- A subspace is less than another if and only if it is less than or equal to the second subspace
547 and there is a point only in the second. -/
548 theorem lt_iff_le_and_exists (s₁ s₂ : AffineSubspace k P) :
549     s₁ < s₂ ↔ s₁ ≤ s₂ ∧ ∃ p ∈ s₂, p ∉ s₁ := by
550   rw [lt_iff_le_not_ge, not_le_iff_exists]
551 
552 /-- If an affine subspace is nonempty and contained in another with the same direction, they are
553 equal. -/
554 theorem eq_of_direction_eq_of_nonempty_of_le {s₁ s₂ : AffineSubspace k P}
555     (hd : s₁.direction = s₂.direction) (hn : (s₁ : Set P).Nonempty) (hle : s₁ ≤ s₂) : s₁ = s₂ :=
556   let ⟨p, hp⟩ := hn
557   ext_of_direction_eq hd ⟨p, hp, hle hp⟩
558 
559 instance nonempty_sup_left (s₁ s₂ : AffineSubspace k P) [Nonempty s₁] :
560     Nonempty (s₁ ⊔ s₂ : AffineSubspace k P) :=
561   .map (Set.inclusion <| SetLike.le_def.1 le_sup_left) ‹_›
562 
563 instance nonempty_sup_right (s₁ s₂ : AffineSubspace k P) [Nonempty s₂] :
564     Nonempty (s₁ ⊔ s₂ : AffineSubspace k P) :=
565   .map (Set.inclusion <| SetLike.le_def.1 le_sup_right) ‹_›
566 
567 variable (k V)
568 
569 /-- The affine span is the `sInf` of subspaces containing the given points. -/
570 theorem affineSpan_eq_sInf (s : Set P) :
571     affineSpan k s = sInf { s' : AffineSubspace k P | s ⊆ s' } :=
572   le_antisymm (affineSpan_le_of_subset_coe <| Set.subset_iInter₂ fun _ => id)
573     (sInf_le (subset_spanPoints k _))
574 
575 variable (P)
576 
577 /-- The Galois insertion formed by `affineSpan` and coercion back to a set. -/
578 protected def gi : GaloisInsertion (affineSpan k) ((↑) : AffineSubspace k P → Set P) where
579   choice s _ := affineSpan k s
580   gc s₁ _s₂ :=
581     ⟨fun h => Set.Subset.trans (subset_spanPoints k s₁) h, affineSpan_le_of_subset_coe⟩
582   le_l_u _ := subset_spanPoints k _
583   choice_eq _ _ := rfl
584 
585 /-- The span of the empty set is `⊥`. -/
586 @[simp]
587 theorem span_empty : affineSpan k (∅ : Set P) = ⊥ :=
588   (AffineSubspace.gi k V P).gc.l_bot
589 
590 /-- The span of `univ` is `⊤`. -/
591 @[simp]
592 theorem span_univ : affineSpan k (Set.univ : Set P) = ⊤ :=
593   eq_top_iff.2 <| subset_affineSpan k _
594 
595 variable {k V P}
596 
597 theorem _root_.affineSpan_le {s : Set P} {Q : AffineSubspace k P} :
598     affineSpan k s ≤ Q ↔ s ⊆ (Q : Set P) :=
599   (AffineSubspace.gi k V P).gc _ _
600 
601 variable (k V) {p₁ p₂ : P}
602 
603 /-- The span of a union of sets is the sup of their spans. -/
604 theorem span_union (s t : Set P) : affineSpan k (s ∪ t) = affineSpan k s ⊔ affineSpan k t :=
605   (AffineSubspace.gi k V P).gc.l_sup
606 
607 /-- The span of a union of an indexed family of sets is the sup of their spans. -/
608 theorem span_iUnion {ι : Type*} (s : ι → Set P) :
609     affineSpan k (⋃ i, s i) = ⨆ i, affineSpan k (s i) :=
610   (AffineSubspace.gi k V P).gc.l_iSup
611 
612 variable (P) in
613 /-- `⊤`, coerced to a set, is the whole set of points. -/
614 @[simp]
615 theorem top_coe : ((⊤ : AffineSubspace k P) : Set P) = Set.univ :=
616   rfl
617 
618 /-- All points are in `⊤`. -/
619 @[simp]
620 theorem mem_top (p : P) : p ∈ (⊤ : AffineSubspace k P) :=
621   Set.mem_univ p
622 
623 @[simp] lemma mk'_top (p : P) : mk' p (⊤ : Submodule k V) = ⊤ := by
624   ext x
625   simp [mem_mk']
626 
627 variable (P)
628 
629 /-- The direction of `⊤` is the whole module as a submodule. -/
630 @[simp]
631 theorem direction_top : (⊤ : AffineSubspace k P).direction = ⊤ := by
632   obtain ⟨p⟩ := S.nonempty
633   ext v
634   refine ⟨imp_intro Submodule.mem_top, fun _hv => ?_⟩
635   have hpv : ((v +ᵥ p) -ᵥ p : V) ∈ (⊤ : AffineSubspace k P).direction :=
636     vsub_mem_direction (mem_top k V _) (mem_top k V _)
637   rwa [vadd_vsub] at hpv
638 
639 /-- `⊥`, coerced to a set, is the empty set. -/
640 @[simp]
641 theorem bot_coe : ((⊥ : AffineSubspace k P) : Set P) = ∅ :=
642   rfl
643 
644 theorem bot_ne_top : (⊥ : AffineSubspace k P) ≠ ⊤ := by
645   intro contra
646   rw [AffineSubspace.ext_iff, bot_coe, top_coe] at contra
647   exact Set.empty_ne_univ contra
648 
649 instance : Nontrivial (AffineSubspace k P) :=
650   ⟨⟨⊥, ⊤, bot_ne_top k V P⟩⟩
651 
652 theorem nonempty_of_affineSpan_eq_top {s : Set P} (h : affineSpan k s = ⊤) : s.Nonempty := by
653   rw [Set.nonempty_iff_ne_empty]
654   rintro rfl
655   rw [AffineSubspace.span_empty] at h
656   exact bot_ne_top k V P h
657 
658 /-- If the affine span of a set is `⊤`, then the vector span of the same set is the `⊤`. -/
659 theorem vectorSpan_eq_top_of_affineSpan_eq_top {s : Set P} (h : affineSpan k s = ⊤) :
660     vectorSpan k s = ⊤ := by rw [← direction_affineSpan, h, direction_top]
661 
662 /-- For a nonempty set, the affine span is `⊤` iff its vector span is `⊤`. -/
663 theorem affineSpan_eq_top_iff_vectorSpan_eq_top_of_nonempty {s : Set P} (hs : s.Nonempty) :
664     affineSpan k s = ⊤ ↔ vectorSpan k s = ⊤ := by
665   refine ⟨vectorSpan_eq_top_of_affineSpan_eq_top k V P, ?_⟩
666   intro h
667   suffices Nonempty (affineSpan k s) by
668     obtain ⟨p, hp : p ∈ affineSpan k s⟩ := this
669     rw [eq_iff_direction_eq_of_mem hp (mem_top k V p), direction_affineSpan, h, direction_top]
670   obtain ⟨x, hx⟩ := hs
671   exact ⟨⟨x, mem_affineSpan k hx⟩⟩
672 
673 /-- For a non-trivial space, the affine span of a set is `⊤` iff its vector span is `⊤`. -/
674 theorem affineSpan_eq_top_iff_vectorSpan_eq_top_of_nontrivial {s : Set P} [Nontrivial P] :
675     affineSpan k s = ⊤ ↔ vectorSpan k s = ⊤ := by
676   rcases s.eq_empty_or_nonempty with hs | hs
677   · simp [hs, subsingleton_iff_bot_eq_top, AddTorsor.subsingleton_iff V P, not_subsingleton]
678   · rw [affineSpan_eq_top_iff_vectorSpan_eq_top_of_nonempty k V P hs]
679 
680 theorem card_pos_of_affineSpan_eq_top {ι : Type*} [Fintype ι] {p : ι → P}
681     (h : affineSpan k (range p) = ⊤) : 0 < Fintype.card ι := by
682   obtain ⟨-, ⟨i, -⟩⟩ := nonempty_of_affineSpan_eq_top k V P h
683   exact Fintype.card_pos_iff.mpr ⟨i⟩
684 
685 -- An instance with better keys for the context
686 instance : Nonempty (⊤ : AffineSubspace k P) := inferInstanceAs (Nonempty (⊤ : Set P))
687 
688 variable {P}
689 
690 /-- No points are in `⊥`. -/
691 theorem notMem_bot (p : P) : p ∉ (⊥ : AffineSubspace k P) :=
692   Set.notMem_empty p
693 
694 instance isEmpty_bot : IsEmpty (⊥ : AffineSubspace k P) :=
695   Subtype.isEmpty_of_false fun _ ↦ notMem_bot _ _ _
696 
697 variable (P)
698 
699 /-- The direction of `⊥` is the submodule `⊥`. -/
700 @[simp]
701 theorem direction_bot : (⊥ : AffineSubspace k P).direction = ⊥ := by
702   rw [direction_eq_vectorSpan, bot_coe, vectorSpan_def, vsub_empty, Submodule.span_empty]
703 
704 variable {k V P}
705 
706 @[simp]
707 theorem coe_eq_bot_iff (Q : AffineSubspace k P) : (Q : Set P) = ∅ ↔ Q = ⊥ :=
708   coe_injective.eq_iff' (bot_coe _ _ _)
709 
710 @[simp]
711 theorem coe_eq_univ_iff (Q : AffineSubspace k P) : (Q : Set P) = univ ↔ Q = ⊤ :=
712   coe_injective.eq_iff' (top_coe _ _ _)
713 
714 theorem nonempty_iff_ne_bot (Q : AffineSubspace k P) : (Q : Set P).Nonempty ↔ Q ≠ ⊥ := by
715   rw [nonempty_iff_ne_empty]
716   exact not_congr Q.coe_eq_bot_iff
717 
718 theorem eq_bot_or_nonempty (Q : AffineSubspace k P) : Q = ⊥ ∨ (Q : Set P).Nonempty := by
719   rw [nonempty_iff_ne_bot]
720   apply eq_or_ne
721 
722 instance [Subsingleton P] : IsSimpleOrder (AffineSubspace k P) where
723   eq_bot_or_eq_top (s : AffineSubspace k P) := by
724     rw [← coe_eq_bot_iff, ← coe_eq_univ_iff]
725     rcases (s : Set P).eq_empty_or_nonempty with h | h
726     · exact .inl h
727     · exact .inr h.eq_univ
728 
729 /-- A nonempty affine subspace is `⊤` if and only if its direction is `⊤`. -/
730 @[simp]
731 theorem direction_eq_top_iff_of_nonempty {s : AffineSubspace k P} (h : (s : Set P).Nonempty) :
732     s.direction = ⊤ ↔ s = ⊤ := by
733   constructor
734   · intro hd
735     rw [← direction_top k V P] at hd
736     refine ext_of_direction_eq hd ?_
737     simp [h]
738   · rintro rfl
739     simp

741 /-- The inf of two affine subspaces, coerced to a set, is the intersection of the two sets of
742 points. -/
743 @[simp]
744 theorem coe_inf (s₁ s₂ : AffineSubspace k P) : (s₁ ⊓ s₂ : Set P) = (s₁ : Set P) ∩ s₂ :=
745   rfl
746 
747 /-- A point is in the inf of two affine subspaces if and only if it is in both of them. -/
748 theorem mem_inf_iff (p : P) (s₁ s₂ : AffineSubspace k P) : p ∈ s₁ ⊓ s₂ ↔ p ∈ s₁ ∧ p ∈ s₂ :=
749   Iff.rfl
750 
751 /-- The direction of the inf of two affine subspaces is less than or equal to the inf of their
752 directions. -/
753 theorem direction_inf (s₁ s₂ : AffineSubspace k P) :
754     (s₁ ⊓ s₂).direction ≤ s₁.direction ⊓ s₂.direction := by
755   simp only [direction_eq_vectorSpan, vectorSpan_def]
756   exact
757     le_inf (sInf_le_sInf fun p hp => trans (vsub_self_mono inter_subset_left) hp)
758       (sInf_le_sInf fun p hp => trans (vsub_self_mono inter_subset_right) hp)
759 
760 /-- If two affine subspaces have a point in common, the direction of their inf equals the inf of
761 their directions. -/
762 theorem direction_inf_of_mem {s₁ s₂ : AffineSubspace k P} {p : P} (h₁ : p ∈ s₁) (h₂ : p ∈ s₂) :
763     (s₁ ⊓ s₂).direction = s₁.direction ⊓ s₂.direction := by
764   ext v
765   rw [Submodule.mem_inf, ← vadd_mem_iff_mem_direction v h₁, ← vadd_mem_iff_mem_direction v h₂, ←
766     vadd_mem_iff_mem_direction v ((mem_inf_iff p s₁ s₂).2 ⟨h₁, h₂⟩), mem_inf_iff]
767 
768 /-- If two affine subspaces have a point in their inf, the direction of their inf equals the inf of
769 their directions. -/
770 theorem direction_inf_of_mem_inf {s₁ s₂ : AffineSubspace k P} {p : P} (h : p ∈ s₁ ⊓ s₂) :
771     (s₁ ⊓ s₂).direction = s₁.direction ⊓ s₂.direction :=
772   direction_inf_of_mem ((mem_inf_iff p s₁ s₂).1 h).1 ((mem_inf_iff p s₁ s₂).1 h).2
773 
774 @[simp, norm_cast]
775 theorem coe_sInf (t : Set (AffineSubspace k P)) :
776     ((sInf t : AffineSubspace k P) : Set P) = ⋂ s ∈ t, s :=
777   rfl
778 
779 theorem mem_sInf_iff (p : P) (t : Set (AffineSubspace k P)) : p ∈ sInf t ↔ ∀ s ∈ t, p ∈ s :=
780   Set.mem_iInter₂
781 
782 theorem direction_sInf (t : Set (AffineSubspace k P)) :
783     direction (sInf t) ≤ ⨅ s ∈ t, s.direction := by
784   simp only [direction_eq_vectorSpan, vectorSpan_def]
785   exact le_iInf₂ fun s hs => Submodule.span_mono <| vsub_self_mono <| biInter_subset_of_mem hs
786 
787 theorem direction_sInf_of_mem (t : Set (AffineSubspace k P)) (p : P) (h : ∀ s ∈ t, p ∈ s) :
788     direction (sInf t) = ⨅ s ∈ t, s.direction := by
789   apply (direction_sInf t).antisymm
790   intro v hv
791   rw [← vadd_mem_iff_mem_direction v ((mem_sInf_iff p t).mpr h), mem_sInf_iff]
792   intro s hs
793   rw [vadd_mem_iff_mem_direction v (h s hs)]
794   simp only [Submodule.mem_iInf] at hv
795   exact hv s hs
796 
797 theorem direction_sInf_of_mem_sInf (t : Set (AffineSubspace k P)) (p : P) (h : p ∈ sInf t) :
798     direction (sInf t) = ⨅ s ∈ t, s.direction :=
799   direction_sInf_of_mem t p <| (mem_sInf_iff p t).mp h
800 
801 @[simp, norm_cast]
802 theorem coe_iInf (s : ι → AffineSubspace k P) :
803     ((iInf s : AffineSubspace k P) : Set P) = ⋂ i, s i := by
804   rw [iInf, coe_sInf, Set.biInter_range]
805 
806 theorem mem_iInf_iff (s : ι → AffineSubspace k P) (p : P) : p ∈ iInf s ↔ ∀ i, p ∈ s i := by
807   rw [iInf, mem_sInf_iff, Set.forall_mem_range]
808 
809 theorem direction_iInf (s : ι → AffineSubspace k P) :
810     (iInf s).direction ≤ ⨅ i, (s i).direction := by
811   apply (direction_sInf _).trans_eq
812   rw [iInf_range]
813 
814 theorem direction_iInf_of_mem (s : ι → AffineSubspace k P) (p : P) (h : ∀ i, p ∈ s i) :
815     (iInf s).direction = ⨅ i, (s i).direction := by
816   rw [iInf, direction_sInf_of_mem _ p ?_, iInf_range]
817   rwa [Set.forall_mem_range]
818 
819 theorem direction_iInf_of_mem_iInf (s : ι → AffineSubspace k P) (p : P) (h : p ∈ iInf s) :
820     (iInf s).direction = ⨅ i, (s i).direction := by
821   rw [iInf, direction_sInf_of_mem_sInf _ p h, iInf_range]
822 
823 /-- If one affine subspace is less than or equal to another, the same applies to their
824 directions. -/
825 theorem direction_le {s₁ s₂ : AffineSubspace k P} (h : s₁ ≤ s₂) : s₁.direction ≤ s₂.direction := by
826   simp only [direction_eq_vectorSpan, vectorSpan_def]
827   exact vectorSpan_mono k h
828 
829 /-- The sup of the directions of two affine subspaces is less than or equal to the direction of
830 their sup. -/
831 theorem sup_direction_le (s₁ s₂ : AffineSubspace k P) :
832     s₁.direction ⊔ s₂.direction ≤ (s₁ ⊔ s₂).direction := by
833   simp only [direction_eq_vectorSpan, vectorSpan_def]
834   exact
835     sup_le
836       (sInf_le_sInf fun p hp => Set.Subset.trans (vsub_self_mono (le_sup_left : s₁ ≤ s₁ ⊔ s₂)) hp)
837       (sInf_le_sInf fun p hp => Set.Subset.trans (vsub_self_mono (le_sup_right : s₂ ≤ s₁ ⊔ s₂)) hp)
838 
839 /-- The sup of the directions of two nonempty affine subspaces with empty intersection is less than
840 the direction of their sup. -/
841 theorem sup_direction_lt_of_nonempty_of_inter_empty {s₁ s₂ : AffineSubspace k P}
842     (h1 : (s₁ : Set P).Nonempty) (h2 : (s₂ : Set P).Nonempty) (he : (s₁ ∩ s₂ : Set P) = ∅) :
843     s₁.direction ⊔ s₂.direction < (s₁ ⊔ s₂).direction := by
844   obtain ⟨p₁, hp₁⟩ := h1
845   obtain ⟨p₂, hp₂⟩ := h2
846   rw [SetLike.lt_iff_le_and_exists]
847   use sup_direction_le s₁ s₂, p₂ -ᵥ p₁,
848     vsub_mem_direction ((le_sup_right : s₂ ≤ s₁ ⊔ s₂) hp₂) ((le_sup_left : s₁ ≤ s₁ ⊔ s₂) hp₁)
849   intro h
850   rw [Submodule.mem_sup] at h
851   rcases h with ⟨v₁, hv₁, v₂, hv₂, hv₁v₂⟩
852   rw [← sub_eq_zero, sub_eq_add_neg, neg_vsub_eq_vsub_rev, add_comm v₁, add_assoc, ←
853     vadd_vsub_assoc, ← neg_neg v₂, add_comm, ← sub_eq_add_neg, ← vsub_vadd_eq_vsub_sub,
854     vsub_eq_zero_iff_eq] at hv₁v₂
855   refine Set.Nonempty.ne_empty ?_ he
856   use v₁ +ᵥ p₁, vadd_mem_of_mem_direction hv₁ hp₁
857   rw [hv₁v₂]
858   exact vadd_mem_of_mem_direction (Submodule.neg_mem _ hv₂) hp₂
859 
860 /-- If the directions of two nonempty affine subspaces span the whole module, they have nonempty
861 intersection. -/
862 theorem inter_nonempty_of_nonempty_of_sup_direction_eq_top {s₁ s₂ : AffineSubspace k P}
863     (h1 : (s₁ : Set P).Nonempty) (h2 : (s₂ : Set P).Nonempty)
864     (hd : s₁.direction ⊔ s₂.direction = ⊤) : ((s₁ : Set P) ∩ s₂).Nonempty := by
865   by_contra h
866   rw [Set.not_nonempty_iff_eq_empty] at h
867   have hlt := sup_direction_lt_of_nonempty_of_inter_empty h1 h2 h
868   rw [hd] at hlt
869   exact not_top_lt hlt
870 
871 /-- If the directions of two nonempty affine subspaces are complements of each other, they intersect
872 in exactly one point. -/
873 theorem inter_eq_singleton_of_nonempty_of_isCompl {s₁ s₂ : AffineSubspace k P}
874     (h1 : (s₁ : Set P).Nonempty) (h2 : (s₂ : Set P).Nonempty)
875     (hd : IsCompl s₁.direction s₂.direction) : ∃ p, (s₁ : Set P) ∩ s₂ = {p} := by
876   obtain ⟨p, hp⟩ := inter_nonempty_of_nonempty_of_sup_direction_eq_top h1 h2 hd.sup_eq_top
877   use p
878   ext q
879   rw [Set.mem_singleton_iff]
880   constructor
881   · rintro ⟨hq1, hq2⟩
882     have hqp : q -ᵥ p ∈ s₁.direction ⊓ s₂.direction :=
883       ⟨vsub_mem_direction hq1 hp.1, vsub_mem_direction hq2 hp.2⟩
884     rwa [hd.inf_eq_bot, Submodule.mem_bot, vsub_eq_zero_iff_eq] at hqp
885   · exact fun h => h.symm ▸ hp
886 
887 /-- Coercing a subspace to a set then taking the affine span produces the original subspace. -/
888 @[simp]
889 theorem affineSpan_coe (s : AffineSubspace k P) : affineSpan k (s : Set P) = s := by
890   refine le_antisymm ?_ (subset_affineSpan _ _)
891   rintro p ⟨p₁, hp₁, v, hv, rfl⟩
892   exact vadd_mem_of_mem_direction hv hp₁
893 
894 end AffineSubspace
895 
896 section AffineSpace'
897 
898 variable (k : Type*) {V : Type*} {P : Type*} [Ring k] [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V]
899   [AffineSpace V P]
900 
901 variable {ι : Type*}
902 
903 open AffineSubspace
904 
905 section
906 
907 variable {s : Set P}
908 
909 /-- The affine span of a set is nonempty if and only if that set is. -/
910 theorem affineSpan_nonempty : (affineSpan k s : Set P).Nonempty ↔ s.Nonempty :=
911   spanPoints_nonempty k s
912 
913 alias ⟨_, _root_.Set.Nonempty.affineSpan⟩ := affineSpan_nonempty
914 
915 /-- The affine span of a nonempty set is nonempty. -/
916 instance [Nonempty s] : Nonempty (affineSpan k s) :=
917   ((nonempty_coe_sort.1 ‹_›).affineSpan _).to_subtype
918 
919 /-- The affine span of a set is `⊥` if and only if that set is empty. -/
920 @[simp]
921 theorem affineSpan_eq_bot : affineSpan k s = ⊥ ↔ s = ∅ := by
922   rw [← not_iff_not, ← Ne, ← Ne, ← nonempty_iff_ne_bot, affineSpan_nonempty,
923     nonempty_iff_ne_empty]
924 
925 @[simp]
926 theorem bot_lt_affineSpan : ⊥ < affineSpan k s ↔ s.Nonempty := by
927   rw [bot_lt_iff_ne_bot, nonempty_iff_ne_empty]
928   exact (affineSpan_eq_bot _).not
929 
930 @[simp]
931 lemma affineSpan_eq_top_iff_nonempty_of_subsingleton [Subsingleton P] :
932     affineSpan k s = ⊤ ↔ s.Nonempty := by
933   rw [← bot_lt_affineSpan k, IsSimpleOrder.bot_lt_iff_eq_top]
934 
935 end
936 
937 variable {k}
938 
939 /-- An induction principle for span membership. If `p` holds for all elements of `s` and is
940 preserved under certain affine combinations, then `p` holds for all elements of the span of `s`. -/
941 @[elab_as_elim]
942 theorem affineSpan_induction {x : P} {s : Set P} {p : P → Prop} (h : x ∈ affineSpan k s)
943     (mem : ∀ x : P, x ∈ s → p x)
944     (smul_vsub_vadd : ∀ (c : k) (u v w : P), p u → p v → p w → p (c • (u -ᵥ v) +ᵥ w)) : p x :=
945   (affineSpan_le (Q := ⟨{x | p x}, smul_vsub_vadd⟩)).mpr mem h
946 
947 /-- A dependent version of `affineSpan_induction`. -/
948 @[elab_as_elim]
949 theorem affineSpan_induction' {s : Set P} {p : ∀ x, x ∈ affineSpan k s → Prop}
950     (mem : ∀ (y) (hys : y ∈ s), p y (subset_affineSpan k _ hys))
951     (smul_vsub_vadd : ∀ (c : k) (u hu v hv w hw), p u hu → p v hv → p w hw →
952       p (c • (u -ᵥ v) +ᵥ w) (AffineSubspace.smul_vsub_vadd_mem _ _ hu hv hw))
953     {x : P} (h : x ∈ affineSpan k s) : p x h := by
954   suffices ∃ (hx : x ∈ affineSpan k s), p x hx from this.elim fun hx hc ↦ hc
955   -- TODO: `induction h using affineSpan_induction` gives the error:
956   -- extra targets for '@affineSpan_induction'
957   -- It seems that the `induction` tactic has decided to ignore the clause
958   -- `using affineSpan_induction` and use `Exists.rec` instead.
959   refine affineSpan_induction h ?mem ?smul_vsub_vadd
960   · exact fun y hy ↦ ⟨subset_affineSpan _ _ hy, mem y hy⟩
961   · exact fun c u v w hu hv hw ↦
962       hu.elim fun hu' hu ↦ hv.elim fun hv' hv ↦ hw.elim fun hw' hw ↦
963         ⟨AffineSubspace.smul_vsub_vadd_mem _ _ hu' hv' hw',
964               smul_vsub_vadd _ _ _ _ _ _ _ hu hv hw⟩
965 
966 variable (k)
967 
968 /-- The difference between two points lies in their `vectorSpan`. -/
969 theorem vsub_mem_vectorSpan_pair (p₁ p₂ : P) : p₁ -ᵥ p₂ ∈ vectorSpan k ({p₁, p₂} : Set P) :=
970   vsub_mem_vectorSpan _ (Set.mem_insert _ _) (Set.mem_insert_of_mem _ (Set.mem_singleton _))
971 
972 /-- The difference between two points (reversed) lies in their `vectorSpan`. -/
973 theorem vsub_rev_mem_vectorSpan_pair (p₁ p₂ : P) : p₂ -ᵥ p₁ ∈ vectorSpan k ({p₁, p₂} : Set P) :=
974   vsub_mem_vectorSpan _ (Set.mem_insert_of_mem _ (Set.mem_singleton _)) (Set.mem_insert _ _)
975 
976 variable {k}
977 
978 /-- A multiple of the difference between two points lies in their `vectorSpan`. -/
979 theorem smul_vsub_mem_vectorSpan_pair (r : k) (p₁ p₂ : P) :
980     r • (p₁ -ᵥ p₂) ∈ vectorSpan k ({p₁, p₂} : Set P) :=
981   Submodule.smul_mem _ _ (vsub_mem_vectorSpan_pair k p₁ p₂)
982 
983 /-- A multiple of the difference between two points (reversed) lies in their `vectorSpan`. -/
984 theorem smul_vsub_rev_mem_vectorSpan_pair (r : k) (p₁ p₂ : P) :
985     r • (p₂ -ᵥ p₁) ∈ vectorSpan k ({p₁, p₂} : Set P) :=
986   Submodule.smul_mem _ _ (vsub_rev_mem_vectorSpan_pair k p₁ p₂)
987 
988 variable (k)
989 
990 /-- The line between two points, as an affine subspace. -/
991 notation "line[" k ", " p₁ ", " p₂ "]" =>
992   affineSpan k (insert p₁ (@singleton _ _ Set.instSingletonSet p₂))
993 
994 /-- The first of two points lies in their affine span. -/
995 theorem left_mem_affineSpan_pair (p₁ p₂ : P) : p₁ ∈ line[k, p₁, p₂] :=
996   mem_affineSpan _ (Set.mem_insert _ _)
997 
998 /-- The second of two points lies in their affine span. -/
999 theorem right_mem_affineSpan_pair (p₁ p₂ : P) : p₂ ∈ line[k, p₁, p₂] :=
1000   mem_affineSpan _ (Set.mem_insert_of_mem _ (Set.mem_singleton _))
1001 
1002 variable {k}
1003 
1004 /-- The span of two points that lie in an affine subspace is contained in that subspace. -/
1005 theorem affineSpan_pair_le_of_mem_of_mem {p₁ p₂ : P} {s : AffineSubspace k P} (hp₁ : p₁ ∈ s)
1006     (hp₂ : p₂ ∈ s) : line[k, p₁, p₂] ≤ s := by
1007   rw [affineSpan_le, Set.insert_subset_iff, Set.singleton_subset_iff]
1008   exact ⟨hp₁, hp₂⟩
1009 
1010 /-- One line is contained in another differing in the first point if the first point of the first
1011 line is contained in the second line. -/
1012 theorem affineSpan_pair_le_of_left_mem {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : p₁ ∈ line[k, p₂, p₃]) :
1013     line[k, p₁, p₃] ≤ line[k, p₂, p₃] :=
1014   affineSpan_pair_le_of_mem_of_mem h (right_mem_affineSpan_pair _ _ _)
1015 
1016 /-- One line is contained in another differing in the second point if the second point of the
1017 first line is contained in the second line. -/
1018 theorem affineSpan_pair_le_of_right_mem {p₁ p₂ p₃ : P} (h : p₁ ∈ line[k, p₂, p₃]) :
1019     line[k, p₂, p₁] ≤ line[k, p₂, p₃] :=
1020   affineSpan_pair_le_of_mem_of_mem (left_mem_affineSpan_pair _ _ _) h
1021 
1022 variable (k)
1023 
1024 /-- `affineSpan` is monotone. -/
1025 @[gcongr, mono]
1026 theorem affineSpan_mono {s₁ s₂ : Set P} (h : s₁ ⊆ s₂) : affineSpan k s₁ ≤ affineSpan k s₂ :=
1027   affineSpan_le_of_subset_coe (Set.Subset.trans h (subset_affineSpan k _))
1028 
1029 /-- Taking the affine span of a set, adding a point and taking the span again produces the same
1030 results as adding the point to the set and taking the span. -/
1031 theorem affineSpan_insert_affineSpan (p : P) (ps : Set P) :
1032     affineSpan k (insert p (affineSpan k ps : Set P)) = affineSpan k (insert p ps) := by
1033   rw [Set.insert_eq, Set.insert_eq, span_union, span_union, affineSpan_coe]
1034 
1035 /-- If a point is in the affine span of a set, adding it to that set does not change the affine
1036 span. -/
1037 theorem affineSpan_insert_eq_affineSpan {p : P} {ps : Set P} (h : p ∈ affineSpan k ps) :
1038     affineSpan k (insert p ps) = affineSpan k ps := by
1039   rw [← mem_coe] at h
1040   rw [← affineSpan_insert_affineSpan, Set.insert_eq_of_mem h, affineSpan_coe]
1041 
1042 variable {k}
1043 
1044 /-- If a point is in the affine span of a set, adding it to that set does not change the vector
1045 span. -/
1046 theorem vectorSpan_insert_eq_vectorSpan {p : P} {ps : Set P} (h : p ∈ affineSpan k ps) :
1047     vectorSpan k (insert p ps) = vectorSpan k ps := by
1048   simp_rw [← direction_affineSpan, affineSpan_insert_eq_affineSpan _ h]
1049 
1050 /-- When the affine space is also a vector space, the affine span is contained within the linear
1051 span. -/
1052 lemma affineSpan_le_toAffineSubspace_span {s : Set V} :
1053     affineSpan k s ≤ (Submodule.span k s).toAffineSubspace := by
1054   intro x hx
1055   simp only [Submodule.mem_toAffineSubspace]
1056   induction hx using affineSpan_induction' with
1057   | mem x hx => exact Submodule.subset_span hx
1058   | smul_vsub_vadd c u _ v _ w _ hu hv hw =>
1059     simp only [vsub_eq_sub, vadd_eq_add]
1060     apply Submodule.add_mem _ _ hw
1061     exact Submodule.smul_mem _ _ (Submodule.sub_mem _ hu hv)
1062 
1063 lemma affineSpan_subset_span {s : Set V} :
1064     (affineSpan k s : Set V) ⊆ Submodule.span k s :=
1065   affineSpan_le_toAffineSubspace_span
1066 
1067 -- TODO: We want this to be simp, but `affineSpan` gets simp-ed away to `spanPoints`!
1068 -- Let's delete `spanPoints`
1069 lemma affineSpan_insert_zero (s : Set V) :
1070     (affineSpan k (insert 0 s) : Set V) = Submodule.span k s := by
1071   rw [← Submodule.span_insert_zero]
1072   refine affineSpan_subset_span.antisymm ?_
1073   rw [← vectorSpan_add_self, vectorSpan_def]
1074   refine Subset.trans ?_ <| subset_add_left _ <| mem_insert ..
1075   gcongr
1076   exact subset_sub_left <| mem_insert ..
1077 
1078 end AffineSpace'
